page: Amazon Web Services c5.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor running at a base clock frequency of 3.6 GHz. Memory capacity is configured at 96.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a 2.0 GB per core compute-optimized ratio. The x86_64 processor implements hardware vector acceleration via AVX, AVX-512, and AVX-512 VNNI extensions, supported by 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1 data cache per core. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs present, and the instance provisions no local instance storage, requiring remote Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent disk storage. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 12 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements place the instance consistently within the middle 50% percentile across multi-core computing workloads. In CPU-focused evaluations, the system recorded a stress-ng multi-core score of 47304.54, a PassMark CPU score of 38880.64, and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12291.0, with single-core Geekbench scoring 1356.0. Memory throughput testing registered 117.04 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 49.12 GB/sec for write operations. Networked key-value throughput achieved 39.58 million Redis SET operations per second, alongside a static web serving throughput of 27.07 GB/sec. Parallelized development workloads executed strongly, registering 33293.0 in Clang software compilation and 70.55 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

Hardware tradeoffs emerge in tasks requiring localized memory density or dedicated acceleration. With no attached NVMe drives or discrete GPUs, data persistence depends entirely on networked storage bandwidth, and large-scale AI tasks exhibit latency bounds. Specifically, large-model (70B) prompt processing generated 6.6 tokens per second, and text generation on smaller models fell into the bottom 25% percentile. However, the balance of 48 dedicated compute threads against 96 GB of memory offers high resource efficiency for compute-dense scenarios that do not require heavy per-core RAM overhead.

The c5.12xlarge instance is optimal for compute-bound workloads, such as distributed CI/CD build environments, batch data processing, ray tracing, parallel scientific simulations, and high-concurrency web servers relying on external databases.
description: Amazon Web Services c5.12xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor operating at 3.6 GHz. Configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs (24 physical cores) and 96.0 GB of DDR4 memory, it delivers a strict 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio suited for computationally demanding workloads. The architecture includes AVX-512 vector instruction extensions, 35 MB of L3 cache, and a 12 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance contains no integrated GPUs and provides no local NVMe storage, relying completely on external network volumes for filesystem storage. Across benchmarks, the server delivers solid multi-threaded performance, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 38880.64 and strong software compilation throughput. While unsuited for GPU computing or memory-bound analytics, its high core density makes it an efficient platform for batch processing, compilation clusters, web serving, and media encoding pipelines.
